audit.why: enemyKit W cd 28/25/22/19/16, untargetable flag; Q/R heal flags.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Gravity Field like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool (W, 28s rank 1): 2s untargetable that eats a whole combo — bait it, then commit into the long downtime. - His Q heals on a 9s-to-4.6s loop: buy Grievous Wounds early. - Guard your W (17s) like a fifth summoner; R for kill windows.

edits.before: E through the wave into his chest, Q-shield the response, empowered-auto, and walk — a full trade where his answer hit a shield.
edits.after: His answer to your step-up is a full-resource Transfusion — cast Q first and the empowered heal-back lands on a shield, not your health bar.

edits.before: Casting E at melee-adjacent range against a loaded engage — Viktor's cast times are an assassin's favorite metronome.
edits.after: Chasing him through side brush burns the tempo your augments need — he pools your catch and heals the walk back for free.

edits.before: Through 4-5 your longer Death Ray out-pokes his heal if you land it clean.
edits.after: Through 4-5 your longer Hextech Ray out-pokes his heal if you land it clean.

edits.before: You control this window: Death Ray out-ranges his Transfusion (Q) and pokes him faster than his heal can recover if you catch him stepping up. His early is weak and mana-starved, so punish every Q he throws at a minion and keep him low before he stacks health.
edits.after: You control this window: Hextech Ray out-ranges his Transfusion (Q) and pokes him faster than his heal can recover if you catch him stepping up. His early is weak and resource-starved, so punish every Q he throws at a minion and keep him low before he stacks health.

edits.before: His Hemoplague (R) plus Sanguine Pool (W) gives him a safe all-in and pool-dodge on your key spells, so the lane evens out — he can pool your Death Ray or Gravity Field and heal through your poke. Bait his pool before committing your combo.
edits.after: His Hemoplague (R) plus Sanguine Pool (W) gives him a safe all-in and pool-dodge on your key spells, so the lane evens out — he can pool your Hextech Ray or Gravity Field and heal through your poke. Bait his pool before committing your combo.

edits.before: Vladimir spikes at his first item as he starts sustaining through your poke and out-healing lane damage, so the trade becomes skill: land clean Death Rays and he can't windup, miss and he heals it back.
edits.after: Vladimir spikes at his first item as he starts sustaining through your poke and out-healing lane damage, so the trade becomes skill: land clean Hextech Rays and he can't windup, miss and he heals it back.

edits.before: You out-scale into two-plus items because evolved Death Ray plus Chaos Storm out-DPS his sustain and he has to dive your frontline to reach you; zone him with Gravity Field and he can't pool out of a committed fight.
edits.after: You out-scale into two-plus items because evolved Hextech Ray plus Chaos Storm out-DPS his sustain and he has to dive your frontline to reach you; zone him with Gravity Field and he can't pool out of a committed fight.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 favour you: Vladimir's early is notoriously weak and mana-hungry, so you free-poke him with autos and Death Ray while his Transfusion heal is small. Keep the wave neutral and clip him every time he walks up to Q a minion. Deny his health-stacking tempo now, because the longer the game goes the harder he is to punish.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 favour you: Vladimir's early is notoriously weak, so you free-poke him with autos and Hextech Ray while his Transfusion heal is small. Keep the wave neutral and clip him every time he walks up to Q a minion. Deny his health-stacking tempo now, because the longer the game goes the harder he is to punish.

edits.before: Through levels 3-5 you keep the edge: your Death Ray out-ranges his Transfusion and your poke outpaces his heal if you land it cleanly. The one thing to respect is Sanguine Pool — he can pool your Death Ray or a committed combo, so don't waste key spells into an obvious pool. Shove him in and build a lead before his first item flips his sustain online.
edits.after: Through levels 3-5 you keep the edge: your Hextech Ray out-ranges his Transfusion and your poke outpaces his heal if you land it cleanly. The one thing to respect is Sanguine Pool — he can pool your Hextech Ray or a committed combo, so don't waste key spells into an obvious pool. Shove him in and build a lead before his first item flips his sustain online.

edits.before: At level 6 and first item the lane evens as Hemoplague and stacked sustain let him heal through your poke and all-in safely, so clean spell landing decides trades. Into two-plus items you out-scale him: evolved Death Ray and Chaos Storm out-DPS his drain, and since he must dive your frontline to reach you, Gravity Field locks him out of the fight once he commits. Play from range and don't let him free-heal.
